title: Local finite presentation is invariant under flat nilpotent deformation
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal with $I^N=0$ for some integer $N\geq1$, and $f:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a flat morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-flat-morphism]. Write $f_0:Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ for its base change [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $f$ is locally of finite presentation if and only if $f_0$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. No Noetherian or prior finite-type assumption is imposed on $A$ or $Y$.

source.place: Tag 06AG, lemma-deform-property, clause (13), with X prime = Y, Y prime = S prime = Spec A, and S = Spec(A/I).

proof.text: Put $A_0=A/I$. For any affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$, its inverse image $U_0$ in $Y_0$ is $U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}A_0$: this follows by restricting the universal property of the fibre product. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A_0\otimes_A B)=\operatorname{Spec}(B/IB)$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A_0$. Explicitly the ring identification sends $\bar a\otimes b$ to $ab\bmod IB$, with inverse $b\bmod IB\mapsto1\otimes b$; the inverse is well-defined since $1\otimes ib=\bar i\otimes b=0$. The two composites are identities by tensor balancing. As $U$ ranges through an affine open cover of $Y$, the $U_0$ cover $Y_0$.

source.place: Tag 06AG, lemma-deform-property, general remark (I), specialized to an affine base

proof.text: Suppose first that $f$ is locally of finite presentation. By [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$ has $B$ finitely presented over $A$, taking the target affine open to be all of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] gives finite presentation of $A_0\otimes_A B$ over $A_0$. Step 1 identifies this with the coordinate ring of $U_0$. These affine opens cover $Y_0$, so the pointwise definition [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] proves that $f_0$ is locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 06AG, lemma-deform-property, initial base-change direction; Tag 05G5, lemma-base-change-finiteness (4)

proof.text: Conversely suppose that $f_0$ is locally of finite presentation, and fix any affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], the hypothesis that $f$ is flat implies that $B$ is a flat $A$-module; no finite-type hypothesis enters this assertion. Step 1 identifies $U_0$ as the affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B_0$ of $Y_0$, where $B_0=B/IB$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] to $f_0$, $U_0$ and the whole affine base $\operatorname{Spec}A_0$: the $A_0$-algebra $B_0$ is finitely presented.

source.place: Tag 06AG, lemma-deform-property, general remark (I) and clause (13)

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], a finite presentation of $B_0$ in particular supplies finitely many algebra generators, so $A_0\to B_0$ is of finite type. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-lift-nilpotent] to $A\to B$ and the ideal $I$, using $I^N=0$ and $N\geq1$. Thus $B$ is generated as an $A$-algebra by finitely many elements $b_1,\ldots,b_n$. The polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] gives a surjection $\pi:P=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to B$, $x_j\mapsto b_j$. Put $K=\ker\pi$. Then $0\to K\to P\to B\to0$ is exact as a sequence of $A$-modules, simply by the definition of a kernel and surjectivity of $\pi$.

source.place: Tag 06AG, lemma-deform-property, clauses (11) and (13); Tag 09ZW, lemma-thicken-property-morphisms-cartesian, finite-type algebra argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] to this short exact sequence, with $R=A$, flat last term $M=B$, and tensor factor $A_0$. It gives an exact sequence $0\to A_0\otimes_A K\to A_0\otimes_A P\to A_0\otimes_A B\to0$. For any $A$-module $M$ the balanced maps $\bar a\otimes m\mapsto am\bmod IM$ and $m\bmod IM\mapsto1\otimes m$ are inverse, since $1\otimes im=\bar i\otimes m=0$. Apply this to $M=K,P,B$. Coefficientwise reduction identifies $P/IP$ with $P_0=A_0[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$: its kernel consists exactly of polynomials whose finitely many coefficients lie in $I$, hence is $IP$. The resulting exact sequence is $0\to K/IK\to P_0\xrightarrow{\pi_0}B_0\to0$, with $k\bmod IK\mapsto k\bmod IP$. In particular this identifies $K/IK$, as a $P_0$-module, with $\ker\pi_0$. This is where flatness is essential; the injection is not inferred merely from right exactness.

source.place: Tag 06AG, lemma-deform-property, clause (13), tensoring the presentation; Tag 00HL, lemma-flat-tor-zero

proof.text: The reduction $\pi_0:P_0\to B_0$ is a surjection of $A_0$-algebras and $B_0$ is finitely presented over $A_0$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-surjection-kernel-fg] supplies finitely many generators $h_1,\ldots,h_m$ of its kernel as an ideal of $P_0$. By step 5 each $h_j$ is the reduction of some $g_j\in K$; choose these lifts. Since $P\to P_0$ is surjective (lift the finitely many coefficients of a polynomial), the $P$-linear map $v:P^{\oplus m}\to K$, $(c_j)\mapsto\sum_jc_jg_j$, is surjective modulo $I$: its reduction has image all of $K/IK$, by the stated generation of $\ker\pi_0$ and the $P_0$-linear identification in step 5.

source.place: Tag 06AG, lemma-deform-property, clause (13), choosing lifted relations; Tag 00R2, lemma-finite-presentation-independent

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-nilpotent] with ring $P$, ideal $J=IP$, source module $P^{\oplus m}$, target module $K$, and map $v$. Here $J^N=0$: expanding a product of $N$ elements from $IP$ puts every coefficient in $I^N=0$. Moreover $JK=IK$, since multiplying an element of $IP$ by an element of the ideal $K$ is a sum of terms $i(pk)$ with $pk\in K$, and the reverse inclusion is immediate. Thus the reduction of $v$ modulo $J$ is exactly the surjection from step 6. Nilpotent Nakayama, which assumes no module finiteness, makes $v$ surjective. Consequently $K=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ as an ideal of $P$.

source.place: Tag 06AG, lemma-deform-property, clause (13), final sentence; Tag 00DV, lemma-NAK (11)

proof.text: It follows that $B\cong A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$: the map induced by $\pi$ is surjective, and its kernel is zero because the ideal of relations is precisely $K$. This is a finite presentation of $B$ over $A$ by [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Since $U$ was any affine open of $Y$, these presentations provide affine neighbourhoods at every point. The definition [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with target affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$, shows that $f$ is locally of finite presentation, completing the reverse implication.

source.place: Tag 06AG, lemma-deform-property, clause (13), conclusion on affine charts

proof_origin.place: Tag 06AG, lemma-deform-property, clause (13), with its finite-type step (11); the same proof works directly for I^N=0, using Tags 00HL, 00R2 and 00DV (11).
